q: NACFE's 2023 white paper laid out a suggested sequence for fleets choosing a powertrain (start with BEV, then hydrogen fuel cell, then natural gas/hybrids/renewable fuels, then efficient diesel as a fallback), while also acknowledging this was 'an oversimplification.' expect: The 2023 white paper's 'Framework for Powertrain Decision Making' (Figure 15) suggests fleets start with BEV, fall back to hydrogen fuel cell, then natural gas/hybrids/renewable fuels, and finally efficient diesel, while explicitly noting fleets will likely need multiple, duty-cycle-specific decisions rather than one universal answer. NACFE reused this same framework graphic in the 2025 Run on Less – Messy Middle report, and that Run's real-world findings confirmed the 2023 premise rather than crowning one winner: 'the real-world results are that all four technologies are performing well in this segment of the market and there is no one right choice for all fleets. Rather powertrain choice depends on the intricacies of each fleet's operation, the length of haul, access to fueling/charging and a host of other factors.'
